hook.text: A barcode needs a direct line-of-sight scan. An RFID tag can be read through a cardboard box at 10 meters.

buildup.text: Barcodes are cheap and universal. RFID tags cost more but offer hands-free, bulk scanning capabilities.

discovery.text: RFID reads hundreds of tags per second without opening boxes—perfect for receiving and inventory counts.

twist.text: RFID tags still cost 5–15 cents each. For low-value goods, that adds up and eats into margins.

climax.text: Retailers like Zara use RFID on every garment—cutting inventory counts from days to hours.

punchline.text: Barcodes are cheap. RFID is fast. Both have a place.

quiz.question: What is RFID's main advantage over barcodes?
options: Can be read without line-of-sight and in bulk
